problemStatement.formal:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that the lower density of $A+A$ is at least $1-\epsilon$ and yet $1_A\ast 1_A(n) \ll_\epsilon 1$ for all $n$?



A similar question can be asked for upper density.

See also [28].
problemStatement.plain: Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that the lower density of $A+A$ is at least $1-\epsilon$ and yet $1_A\ast 1_A(n) \ll_\epsilon 1$ for all $n$?
whyMatters: The question probes the relationship between additive structure (a sumset of nearly full lower density) and additive uniformity (representation function bounded by O(1)) — a regime where Plünnecke-Ruzsa-style methods break down
Connects directly to Erdős-Turán additive bases conjecture (#28): if r_A is bounded yet A+A has positive density, A is much sparser than required by additive bases
Sidon sets show density 0, so the gap between bounded representations and density 1-ε is exactly the question of how additive structure scales
Either answer would be deep: a YES construction (positive answer) would build a near-tile of N with optimally bounded sums; a NO would be a finite-r reverse Plünnecke result

proven: Sidon sets have upper density 0 — directly from the |A ∩ [1,N]|² ≤ 4N counting bound
Plünnecke-Ruzsa: if |A+A| ≤ K|A|, then |kA| ≤ K^k |A| for all k ≥ 1 — links additive structure to representation count
Erdős-Turán (1941): for any infinite Sidon set A, the counting function |A ∩ [1,N]| = O(√N) (up to log)
open: Main question: Does there exist A ⊆ ℕ with lower density of A+A ≥ 1-ε and r_A(n) = O_ε(1) for all n?
Upper-density variant: same question with upper density
Erdős-Turán additive bases conjecture (#28): an additive basis of order 2 cannot have r_A bounded — see erdos_turan_conjecture_28 axiom in this file
knownResults.goal: Formalize the density and representation-function definitions, prove that Sidon sets answer no (they have density 0), and document the open conjecture without making false formal claims.
